commands.name: acme
commands.reference_description: Documented RFC 7638/8555 contracts using published P-256 generator coordinates and independently encoded JWK/SHA-256/base64url values. JWS envelope segments are fixed expectations, and an independent Python integer implementation verifies each randomized ES256 signature against the known public point. These are contract cases, not external CLI parity.

cases.purpose: Check Bash reports acme as a builtin and help exposes its documented contract; the expected marker is emitted only after all documentation checks pass.
Check scalar one maps to the published P-256 generator point and that the canonical JWK uses RFC 7638 member names and unpadded base64url coordinates.
Check the RFC 7638 thumbprint for scalar one, independently computed as base64url(SHA-256(canonical JWK JSON)).
Check RFC 8555 keyAuthorization concatenates the supplied challenge token, one period, and the independently calculated JWK thumbprint.
Check the documented jws-extract-key-authorization alias returns the same RFC 8555 value for a distinct token.

Check flattened JWS framing for a new-account style jwk header and inline JSON payload. The fixed protected and payload segments are independently base64url encoded; the random signature must be 64-byte JOSE raw form encoded without padding. An independent Python integer implementation also verifies ES256 against the published P-256 generator point and checks canonical signature encoding.

Check the account kid header and -f payload path preserve binary fixture bytes including NUL and 0xff. Header/payload encodings are independent RFC base64url values; signature shape is checked without claiming independent cryptographic verification. An independent Python integer implementation also verifies ES256 against the published P-256 generator point and checks canonical signature encoding.

Check the documented POST-as-GET form uses the empty base64url payload segment when neither -d nor -f is supplied, with a kid header and valid JOSE raw-signature encoding. An independent Python integer implementation also verifies ES256 against the published P-256 generator point and checks canonical signature encoding.
Check malformed private-key length is rejected with EX_USAGE (2), while keeping the test script itself successful after capturing the expected command failure.
Check the documented --jwk/--kid exclusion returns EX_USAGE (2) before attempting a network or ACME operation.
Full ACME directory, account, order, challenge, finalize, and certificate issuance behavior is outside this crypto-only loadable and cannot be exercised against a live service in this suite.

commands.name: index
commands.reference_description: Git's documented index behavior: git update-index --index-info creates and updates entries, git ls-files --stage lists them, and git update-index --add/--force-remove/--refresh provide the operation counterparts. The metadata contract uses Bash type/help builtins and the documented index help text.

cases.purpose: Bash must register index as a builtin and expose its documented help, including the atomic-write and update-stat verbs.

Check read output, the list synonym, and -V array contents against Git's staged listing for entries in path and stage order.
Apply textual index-info records that remove a path, add a conflict stage, replace all conflict stages with stage zero, and add another path; compare both the listing and resulting index file.

Add an empty working file from its known Git blob ID, list it, remove it, and list again. compare_tree is disabled because Git stores the empty blob object and both indexes record sandbox-specific inode and timestamp fields while the builtin receives the blob ID from its caller. Refresh an unchanged entry and compare mode/blob/stage/path with Git. Independently decode every stored stat field, verify it against os.stat of the private working file, verify SHA-1 trailer and lock/temp cleanup. compare_tree is disabled because raw inode, timestamps and Git object storage differ inherently; those stat fields are explicitly checked against each side's independent filesystem observations.
Validate rollback and lock/temp cleanup when an atomic index replacement fails at different I/O stages.
Write the canonical empty v2 index and read it back; compare the complete binary header/count/SHA-1 trailer with an independently encoded Git-format contract, including no lock/temp residue.
Read a valid Git v2 index constructed independently from the published binary format, covering stdout/list/array APIs without candidate writer dependence.

Check GNU's default command-line symlink-to-directory behavior against -d's link listing and -L's dereferenced directory listing.

Check a nonempty diagnostic for a missing command-line operand while checking that a valid operand is still listed and serious trouble returns status 2. Diagnostic prefixes identify the builtin and need not reproduce an external executable name.
Check invalid long-option status, no stdout, and a nonempty usage diagnostic for option parsing errors. Diagnostic prefixes identify the builtin and need not reproduce an external executable name.

commands.name: mouse
commands.reference_description: No GNU mouse CLI exists. X10 encodes button and coordinates with a +32 offset; these vectors check the inverse transform plus shift and release interpretation.
Wire 32/33/34 normalize to button codes 0/1/2; coordinates remain 1-based decimal values.

Also checks that failed longer fallback attempts cannot leak their time fields into a shorter successful prefix match; 1704153600 is calendar midnight UTC. The malformed-seconds example keeps the valid 12:34 prefix (1704198840), with a warning. A failed hour/minute attempt followed by a date-only match must reset the partially assigned hour and yield midnight.

commands.name: tar
commands.reference_description: Parity cases run the same script under system Bash and GNU tar from the runner reference PATH. Three static archive payloads are generated independently with Python standard-library tarfile in USTAR/PAX formats; GNU tar validates their expected listing, extraction, mode and link behavior. Archive bytes are not asserted because the documented contract excludes byte-identical tar/gzip encodings. Creation cases compare round-trip results; independently encoded USTAR/PAX/gzip inputs establish read-side interoperability only.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata reports the registered tar loadable as a builtin; this checks shell integration, not GNU tar behavior.

Traditional tar cf syntax creates a recursive archive containing a long PAX path and symlink; GNU tar output, extraction tree, modes and -C working-directory restoration are compared. Archive bytes are removed because the documented contract excludes byte-identical encodings. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.

Extracts a fixed USTAR archive encoded independently with Python tarfile, covering a directory, binary file, symbolic link and hard link; GNU tar listings and extracted filesystem/link relationships are the oracle.
Reads a fixed POSIX PAX archive encoded independently with Python tarfile; its overlong path requires the PAX path record, and GNU tar supplies expected listing, stdout extraction, status and tree.

Creates, lists and extracts a gzip-compressed tar stream with a NUL-containing payload; GNU tar plus its gzip dependency is the reference, while archive bytes are removed because compression encodings may differ. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.

Checks GNU --strip-components path rewriting during extraction and verifies the selected member can still be read to stdout; the archive is removed so only resulting fixture files are compared. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.

Checks GNU --no-recursion archives and extracts the named directory entry without its child tree; GNU tar listing and resulting tree define the expected behavior. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
Extracts the same independently encoded USTAR member once with default umask handling and once with -p under umask 077; GNU tar establishes both resulting file modes.

Checks the documented -C restoration contract after a missing relative directory and records GNU tar statuses for both that failure and a missing -O member. The printed statuses are compared against GNU tar; the final process status is the -C failure status.

Archives two names for one source inode and extracts them; GNU tar preserves the hard-link relationship, so a difference from the documented implementation behavior that writes separate regular members remains a failing tree comparison. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.

Uses only a private relative FIFO fixture. GNU tar can archive and extract FIFOs; this exercises the real GNU CLI contract and must expose candidate rejection if present. Both encoding and decoding use the same implementation on each side; this is a round-trip-result comparison, not independent decoding of candidate archives.
Character and block device tar entries are outside the private regular-file fixture contract.
Read independently encoded USTAR compressed with Python gzip; GNU tar validates listing, binary payload, permissions, symlinks and hardlinks. This establishes compressed input interoperability.

An overlong first hardlink path requires PAX linkpath on a recursive alias. Archive a FIFO sibling too; both the builtin and independent GNU tar decode the result before full topology/mode/data comparison.
Repeated regular operands emit GNU-compatible hardlink members without unlinking their own target; strip-components rewrites the hardlink name and target consistently.
The writer remembers logical member names across -C changes, then starts a fresh hardlink context for another archive in the same shell.
A missing operand after a first hardlink member fails archive creation; the next same-shell archive remains self-contained and does not reference a prior archive path.
Decode a fixed Python-authored USTAR FIFO and following regular member under umask077, once normally and once with -p. Following file creation verifies umask restoration.
Establish GNU writer behavior when a second inode replaces the first inode archive pathname before an alias of the first inode is written; decode with independent GNU tar.

declared_coverage: Bash builtin registration metadata contract.
Traditional cf syntax, recursive creation, PAX long names, symlinks, listing, -O, and -C cwd restoration.
Independent USTAR extraction of regular, directory, symlink and hard-link entries.
Independent PAX path-record extraction for a basename beyond ustar limits.
Gzip tar create/list/extract and binary member output.
Failed -C cwd restoration, missing-member error status, hard-link creation semantics, and private FIFO archive behavior.
exclusions: Append/update, sparse formats, unsafe or absolute member/link paths, device nodes, and exact archive/compression bytes are not asserted.
Device-node parity is deferred pending an isolated synthetic mknod/stat fixture or reviewed syscall mock.

Only stable ordinary regular-file hardlinks and FIFO metadata are extended. Character/block devices, copy-mode special files, concurrent mutation, forward hardlinks, fault injection and exhaustive archive dialects remain outside this coverage.

Distinct source inodes mapped onto one archive pathname can make a later hardlink alias bind to the replacement data, as independently observed with GNU tar. General preservation of source data/topology across conflicting archive member names is not claimed.

deferrals.purpose: Exercise non-root allow, deny, non-interactive deny, and interactive verification behavior at the authority boundary.

deferrals.purpose: Cover --partx-kernel BLKPG add/delete/update and post-write partition reread behavior.
deferrals.reason: BLKPG and BLKRRPART require CAP_SYS_ADMIN on a real block device (block/ioctl.c blkpg_do_ioctl/blkdev_reread_part), and uid 2000 with setgroups([]) cannot open /dev/loop-control or /dev/loopN (root:disk 0660), cannot mknod block nodes (CAP_MKNOD; device nodes are refused inside user namespaces), and the real virtio disk nodes are root:disk 0660, so no block device with known contents is visible to an unprivileged fixture. Loop devices also need LO_FLAGS_PARTSCAN for kernel partitions. r3 argument/uid checks need neither.
remaining_requirements: --partx-kernel add DEV [MIN MAX] issues BLKPG_ADD_PARTITION for each table entry in range so the kernel partition set (/sys/block/loopN/loopNpM start/size) matches the on-disk MBR/GPT, like util-linux partx --add.
--partx-kernel delete and update remove/resize kernel partitions in range; update requires geometry; MIN>MAX and out-of-range bounds are rejected.
Non-root refusal: as uid != 0 the command fails with 'BLKPG mutation requires uid 0' before opening the device (fdisk.c:2969-2972); a regular-file image as root fails with 'is not a block device'.
Post-write partition reread: after a table write on a block device the candidate issues BLKRRPART (fdisk.c:2849) and the kernel partition set reflects the new table; warnings for EBUSY are printed.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

Resulting image bytes after w are independently decoded (MBR entries, signature) and unchanged after q.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Exercise exact cold, resident, and page-boundary counts for mincore-based reporting.
deferrals.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: Not observable without privilege in the parity VM (probe-fincore-69): mincore(2) reports every page resident for files the caller cannot write (mm/mincore.c can_do_mincore), util-linux fincore cachestat(2) returns EPERM for non-owned files, and every writable scratch area is tmpfs, where POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED evicts nothing. Needs a caller-owned file on a writable non-tmpfs filesystem (root-provisioned ext4 scratch or BLOCK-DEV).; r4: Not observable without privilege in the parity VM (probe-fincore-69): mincore(2) reports every page resident for files the caller cannot write (mm/mincore.c can_do_mincore), util-linux fincore cachestat(2) returns EPERM for non-owned files, and every writable scratch area is tmpfs, where POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED evicts nothing. Needs a caller-owned file on a writable non-tmpfs filesystem (root-provisioned ext4 scratch or BLOCK-DEV).; r5: Not observable without privilege in the parity VM (probe-fincore-69): mincore(2) reports every page resident for files the caller cannot write (mm/mincore.c can_do_mincore), util-linux fincore cachestat(2) returns EPERM for non-owned files, and every writable scratch area is tmpfs, where POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED evicts nothing. Needs a caller-owned file on a writable non-tmpfs filesystem (root-provisioned ext4 scratch or BLOCK-DEV).
remaining_requirements: Cold state: after writeback and POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED on a nonempty private file, fincore reports RES 0 and PAGES 0 with the exact table bytes, matching util-linux fincore.
Partial residency: after DONTNEED, reading exactly one page with POSIX_FADV_RANDOM (no readahead) reports exactly 1 resident page.
Transitions are observed in sequence within one side: cold, then partial, then warm, then cold again.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Qualify behavior when IMAGE is an actual block device rather than a private regular-file fixture.

deferrals.purpose: Convert fixed RTC calendars in UTC to exact seconds with zero nanoseconds, including pre-epoch, leap-century, and 2038 boundary values, while checking syscall order and no setter call for invalid calendars.

deferrals.purpose: Deferred operation check for anonymous and named session creation, including serial output and ensuring all later operations are confined to the newly owned ring.

A trusted python3 ctypes helper calling syscall(SYS_keyctl, KEYCTL_READ/DESCRIBE) reads payloads independently. keyutils is not installed, so there is no CLI byte oracle unless root adds keyutils to image.lock. Hazard: @u and @us name the uid-2000 user keyrings shared across cases and sides, so fixtures must not add to or clear them; alternatively the driver can give each case a distinct uid.

Subsequent add/search/clear in the same shell operate on the new ring (@s resolves to the printed serial)
Join failure is reported (status 1) and no mutation follows

remaining_requirements: ns mount-private after unshare mount makes / recursively private: a mount made in the side is not visible in another namespace (propagation isolation)
ns bind SRC DST binds a fixture directory/file; reads/writes through DST reach SRC
ns bind SRC DST ro produces a read-only bind (second MS_REMOUNT|MS_BIND|MS_RDONLY); writes via DST fail EROFS while SRC stays writable
ns remount-readonly PATH makes an existing mount read-only (EROFS on write)
Kernel refusals without mount privilege (uid 2000 without user namespace) -> EPERM status 1; invalid paths -> ENOENT
Results agree with util-linux mount --bind / -o remount,bind,ro and findmnt
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check the pivot-root syscall wrapper and resulting old-root placement using a disposable root tree.
deferrals.reason: Not a capability block. pivot_root needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN over a private mount namespace, which a USERNS has after it mounts its own tmpfs (tmpfs is FS_USERNS_MOUNT). The new root needs a minimal tree, such as a static busybox-free layout with a bind of /usr. No fixture exists.
remaining_requirements: ns pivot-root NEW PUT_OLD switches the root of the mount namespace; afterwards / is NEW and the old root is visible at PUT_OLD
cwd/root seen by a child after pivot (readlink /proc/self/root, ls /)
Kernel-rejected layout (NEW not a mount point, PUT_OLD outside NEW, shared propagation) -> EINVAL/EBUSY status 1
Comparison with an independent pivot_root helper (util-linux pivot_root command or python3 ctypes syscall)
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check loading and applying a binary sock_filter profile, including valid, malformed, and kernel-rejected profiles.
deferrals.reason: Not a capability block. seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER) is unprivileged with no_new_privs, the legacy runner already sets that through bwrap and does not deny seccomp(), and the filter is irreversible only for the disposable fixture shell. No fixture exists.
remaining_requirements: ns seccomp PROFILE loads a valid allow-all sock_filter program (8-byte instructions) and applies it to the calling shell; /proc/self/status Seccomp: 2
A narrowly denying profile (e.g. uname -> SECCOMP_RET_ERRNO|EDOM) makes a subsequent child uname fail with that errno while other calls work
Empty, mis-sized (not a multiple of 8) and over-limit (>4096 instructions) profiles are rejected before the syscall with status 1
Kernel-rejected program (invalid opcode / bad jump) -> EINVAL status 1
Without NO_NEW_PRIVS and without CAP_SYS_ADMIN, seccomp() returns EACCES
Behavior agrees with an independent seccomp helper loading the same bytes
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check LSM detection and on-exec profile requests for AppArmor and SELinux, including unavailable and invalid-profile paths.
deferrals.reason: The detection and on-exec write paths are file-based and testable unprivileged with the documented root overrides; no fixture exists for them. A real AppArmor transition needs a test profile, and loading one needs CAP_MAC_ADMIN in the initial user namespace with an unload restore, which no driver provides. Missing capability: CAP_MAC_ADMIN in the initial user namespace. Writes to /sys/kernel/security/apparmor/.replace fail with EACCES/EPERM for uid 2000, and USERNS root has no MAC_ADMIN over the global policy. SELinux needs a different boot configuration and policy.
remaining_requirements: ns lsm-detect reports "apparmor: available", "selinux: available" or "none: absent" from securityfs/selinuxfs, and -V binds the kind word
ns lsm-onexec PROFILE writes "exec PROFILE" (AppArmor) or bare PROFILE (SELinux) to <proc>/self/attr/exec; the BASHNS_PROC_ROOT override points at a fixture tree
Absent LSM and invalid profile errors produce diagnostics and status 1
A real AppArmor on-exec transition to a dedicated test profile takes effect at exec (child /proc/self/attr/current shows the profile and its confinement denies a fixture read)
SELinux transition
ns spawn lsm PROFILE applies the onexec request in the child before exec
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check cgroup v2 create, controller value, process membership, controller-enable, and remove behavior.
deferrals.reason: Writing cgroup files needs a writable delegated subtree. As uid 2000, mkdir under root-owned /sys/fs/cgroup returns EACCES; the legacy runner has no /sys. The root controller must create a per-side subtree and chown it to uid 2000 (cgroup delegation: directory, cgroup.procs, cgroup.subtree_control). The candidate hardcodes /sys/fs/cgroup (loadables/ns.c:532), so the fixture must address the subtree by its relative path from the root. Path validation needs no privilege.
remaining_requirements: ns cgroup-create NAME mkdir -p under /sys/fs/cgroup for a relative NAME
ns cgroup-set NAME FILE VALUE writes a controller file (e.g. pids.max) and reads back
ns cgroup-add NAME [PID] writes the pid (default self) to cgroup.procs; /proc/PID/cgroup reflects membership
ns cgroup-enable CONTROLLERS [NAME] writes +ctrl to cgroup.subtree_control
ns cgroup-remove NAME rmdir of an empty cgroup
Relative-path validation rejects absolute, "..", ".", empty components and FILE with "/"
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Exercise query request/reply matching and the normal, alarm, KoD, malformed-response and timeout paths.
deferrals.reason: No executed fixture supplies an RFC 5905 UDP responder with scenario-specific packets; the existing 'udp' peer only echoes 'echo:'+datagram and cannot build NTP packets.
remaining_requirements: Normal reply: query sends a 48-byte mode-3 client packet, matches the reply's originate timestamp to its transmit timestamp, and prints 'offset=... delay=... stratum=N server=IP' with status 0.
A reply whose originate timestamp does not match the request is rejected (not reported as success).
LI=3 (alarm, unsynchronized) reply is rejected with nonzero status.
Stratum-0 Kiss-o'-Death with refid RATE is recognized (RFC 5905 7.4) and reported as KoD/back-off with nonzero status.
Malformed replies (wrong mode, short packet, zero transmit timestamp) are rejected with nonzero status.
No response: query times out within -t MS and returns nonzero without hanging.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Verify multi-server offset aggregation, panic/clamp boundaries and the documented -n applied=no result.
deferrals.reason: No executed fixture provides several deterministic NTP servers; sync uses one BASHNTP_SERVER_PORT for all servers, so distinct loopback addresses are needed.
remaining_requirements: sync -s A -s B -s C queries each server and reports the median offset (odd count) and mean of the middle two (even count).
Panic boundary: |median| > 1024 s is refused with a diagnostic unless --allow-big-jump.
Limit clamp: -l LIMIT refuses to apply an offset beyond the limit ('exceeds limit ... not applying').
-n prints applied=no and performs no clock syscall (CLOCK_REALTIME and adjtimex state unchanged).
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check a serve response's mode/version/leap/stratum/refid and timestamp fields against a fixed client request.
deferrals.reason: No executed fixture sends a client request to a candidate-run ntp serve and decodes the response. The existing udp-client peer sends one text datagram and does not record replies.
remaining_requirements: ntp serve answers a fixed mode-3 request with a mode-4 response echoing the client's version.
Leap indicator, stratum and refid in the response match --leap/--stratum/--refid.
Response originate timestamp equals the request transmit timestamp; receive/transmit timestamps are nonzero and ordered (receive <= transmit).
Serve is bounded by --once/--max N and exits after answering.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check config parsing, cfg/last state records, one-shot completion and the documented dry-run discipline output.
deferrals.reason: No executed fixture provides an NTP responder for run, and no case observes the clock around a dry-run discipline call.
remaining_requirements: ntp run -c CONFIG parses server/interval/retry/timeout/polls/limit/step_threshold/discipline keys and snapshots them to STATEDIR/cfg in the documented key=value form.
After a successful poll STATEDIR/last records offset=, servers=got/total and when=.
--once completes a single iteration and exits with the documented status.
--dry-run-discipline prints the would-apply action line containing live_clock_settime=no live_ntp_adjtime=no for slew/step/kernel disciplines.
No clock mutation occurs in dry-run: CLOCK_REALTIME is not stepped and adjtimex state (offset/status) is unchanged.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Verify the NTS-KE negotiation, cookie handling and authenticated NTP response path against independently generated protocol fixtures.
deferrals.reason: No executed fixture provides an NTS-KE TLS server and an NTS-authenticated NTP UDP responder. The candidate's ntp query passes no CA path to bc_nts_ke_run, so trust must come from the system bundle, which a fixture must override privately.
remaining_requirements: ntp query nts:HOST performs an RFC 8915 NTS-KE TLS 1.3 handshake with ALPN ntske/1, sends Next Protocol (NTPv4), AEAD (AES-SIV-CMAC-256) and End records, and accepts the server's records.
Cookies returned by NTS-KE are consumed: the NTP request carries Unique Identifier, NTS Cookie (and placeholder) extension fields and an authenticator sealed with the exported C2S key.
An authenticated server response (S2C key, matching Unique Identifier, valid authenticator) is accepted and reported as offset/delay/stratum/server.

Negative paths: missing cookie, failed authenticator, wrong unique identifier and NTS-KE failure produce a nonzero status with diagnostics (ntp.c error strings 'nts-ke failed', 'returned no NTP cookie', 'NTS authenticator verification failed').
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Exercise pack cat through an index v2 64-bit offset entry above the 32-bit offset range.
deferrals.reason: The real >2 GiB scenario needs a resource class the VM does not offer. The 64-bit table lookup itself (r1) can be reached with a small pack: an index whose 32-bit entry has the MSB set and points into a one-entry overflow table holding a small offset. Git reads such entries through nth_packed_object_offset, but git verify-pack/fsck may reject an overflow entry below 2^31, so the reference must be recorded rather than assumed.
remaining_requirements: pack cat resolves an object through an index v2 64-bit offset (MSB-set 32-bit entry → overflow table).
The object at offset ≥ 0x80000000 is decoded byte-identically to git cat-file.
verify accepts the overflow table (git verify-pack agrees).
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Future coverage for set, set-fd, change, add, and add-fd password hashing and shadow updates.
deferrals.reason: Remaining obligations: r3: Not executed.; r5: The secret-slot path that uses the device needs /dev/bashos-auth.
remaining_requirements: change verifies the old password before replacing.
Kernel secret-slot path (BASHPASSWD_REQUIRE_KERNEL_SECRETS=1) uses the device.

deferrals.purpose: Future coverage for correct/wrong password results, locked/malformed shadow rows, and failure lockout state.

The Debian guest kernel has no such device and the repository holds only the UAPI header, so open() fails with ENOENT and no unprivileged fixture can observe any ioctl behaviour.
remaining_requirements: Kernel-secret path variant.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Future coverage for prompt ordering, new-password confirmation, echo suppression, and terminal restoration.

The PTY driver (terminal group) supplies the owned terminal; no auth device is required.
remaining_requirements: Prompt ordering for change/set (current, new, confirm).
New-password confirmation mismatch is rejected without updating shadow.
Echo is suppressed during reads.
Terminal restored after success, mismatch, read failure (EOF) and signal interruption (^C).
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check install validation, single-call batching, literal helper argv, and helper exit-status propagation.
deferrals.reason: Never executed, but every obligation is fixture-relative and reachable in the existing legacy runner with a recording mock helper script; no VM-level capability is involved.
remaining_requirements: Valid multiple names listed in INDEX produce exactly one helper call with literal argv [$BASH, INSTALLER, --internal, --root, ROOT, --repo, REPO, --allow-unsigned, install, NAME...] in operand order.
An invalid name (path, leading '-', bad characters) -> status 2 and zero helper calls; a valid name missing from INDEX -> status 1, diagnostic per missing name, zero helper calls; no NAME -> 2.

Helper exit status propagation: helper exit 0 -> 0; exit 3 -> 3 with 'install failed (bl-pkg exit 3)'; helper killed by signal N -> 128+N; missing/non-regular/unreadable installer -> 127/126 before any call.
One-command environment overrides ('PAYLOAD_ROOT=r2 payload install a') and exported variables reach the helper and do not persist in the calling shell.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Check transaction lookup and rollback dispatch without performing a real package rollback.
deferrals.reason: Never executed; all transaction-selection and dispatch obligations are fixture-relative and reachable in the existing legacy runner.
remaining_requirements: remove resolves each NAME's txn from its regular state file before any helper call, and calls '$BASH INSTALLER --internal --root ROOT rollback TXN' once per distinct txn in operand order.
Names sharing one txn trigger one helper call, and each such name reports the shared result ('payload: removed NAME' or the failure).

Refusals: invalid name, not installed, state without txn=, malformed txn (empty, leading '-', whitespace/control bytes, overlong >= field size), non-regular (FIFO/directory) state -> diagnostic, no helper call for that name, final status 1 if nothing failed in a helper.
Partial failure: when one rollback fails, later distinct txns are still attempted, and the first failing helper status is returned.
Nothing outside the private fixture is removed or altered (the mock does not touch state).

deferrals.purpose: Qualify the real image-owned helper's install/remove integration and resulting package state.

deferrals.purpose: Capture a known frame count into a classic pcap file and verify global and per-record fields, snaplen truncation, and output permissions.

Global header fields: magic 0xa1b2c3d4, version 2.4, snaplen = -s, linktype 1.

Output file permissions follow 0644 & ~umask.

deferrals.purpose: Check interface selection and bounded timeout behavior with and without injected packets.

deferrals.purpose: Compare default comm-field regex matching, -x whole-name matching, alternatives, empty patterns, invalid ERE handling, and self-exclusion with GNU procps-ng pgrep.
deferrals.reason: Only the invalid-ERE parser path has GNU parity. Name-ERE semantics are proven on candidate-only synthetic records; GNU procps cannot read BASHOS_PROC_ROOT and no shared process set exists for both sides.
remaining_requirements: Default mode applies a POSIX ERE to the comm field (substring match) and lists matching PIDs, compared with GNU procps-ng pgrep.
-x anchors the ERE to the whole comm name (similar-name exclusion).
Alternatives in the ERE (a|b) and anchored alternatives under -x.
Empty pattern behaviour (matches every process) and its interaction with selectors.
Self-exclusion: the pgrep invocation never reports itself.

deferrals.purpose: Compare -f command-line matching, -a/-l listing, -d delimiters, and -c output, including NUL-separated arguments, embedded newlines, long arguments, and empty command lines.

-a lists PID plus full command line; -l lists PID plus comm.
-d DELIM joins multiple PIDs with the delimiter.
Embedded newline inside an argument is rendered as in procps listing.
Long arguments (beyond 4096 bytes) and empty command lines (kernel threads) are handled.

deferrals.purpose: Compare effective and real UID, GID, parent, process-group and session selectors; comma alternatives and combined selectors; -v; and newest/oldest selection including start-time ties.

Only two sub-obligations need more: a process with ruid != euid (an unprivileged uid-2000 process cannot acquire distinct real/effective IDs; image has no setuid helper and scratch mounts are nosuid) and forced start-time ties (not producible live; unmodified procps reads only /proc).
remaining_requirements: -u (effective UID) and -U (real UID) select different processes when real and effective IDs differ.
-G real GID, -P parent, -g process group, -s session selectors, including 0 meaning own group/session.
Comma alternatives inside one selector and AND-combination across selectors.
-v inverts the match.
-n / -o choose the newest / oldest process, with start-time ties broken by PID.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.

deferrals.purpose: Complete parser option matrix beyond the bounded runnable GNU parser cases.
deferrals.reason: Four parser paths have GNU parity. Selector-argument errors, clustered/attached/long forms, extra positional arguments and help/version are unexercised; the parser cases need no shared process set because they fail before or with an empty enumeration.
remaining_requirements: Selector argument errors: missing value, invalid numeric/user/group value, unknown user name.
Option forms: long options with = and separate values, attached short values, clustered flags (-fc, -fu USER), -- terminator, extra positional argument.
-V/--version and -h/--help statuses and output streams.

deferrals.purpose: Compare -c filtering when one controlled process has the caller's root and another has a different root.

remaining_requirements: -c reports only processes whose root equals the caller's root.
A process with a different root (chroot) is excluded under -c and included without it.

deferrals.purpose: Exercise IPv4 echo request construction, exact reply identity and payload matching, output accounting, and success status with one deterministic matching reply.

Only replies matching identifier, sequence and payload are accepted and counted.
Per-reply output and summary accounting reflect one matching reply; status 0.
Generated request bytes match RFC 792 layout (checksum valid).

deferrals.purpose: Exercise IPv6 echo request/reply type, sequence and payload matching, source validation, and successful accounting.

Echo reply (type 129) matching id/seq/payload from the target source is accepted; replies from another source are ignored.
Successful accounting and status 0.

-w DEADLINE ends a multi-probe run (-c larger than deadline allows) at the deadline with status 1.

deferrals.purpose: Exercise documented minimum/maximum numeric values and representative malformed or out-of-range -c, -W, -w, and -i arguments, checking usage status and that invalid values do not proceed to resolution or socket creation.

remaining_requirements: Documented -w range 0.001..86400 is accepted at both ends and rejected just outside (0, 86401) with usage status.
Malformed numbers ('abc', '1x', empty) for -c, -W, -w, -i are rejected with usage status.
Out-of-range -c, -W, -i values are rejected with usage status.
Rejected arguments do not resolve the host or open a socket.

Destination port-unreachable terminates the trace with status 0 (reached).
Unreached destination after -m MAX_TTL returns status 1.

deferrals.purpose: Cover info and verify for valid, unsigned, untrusted, revoked, tampered, malformed, wrong-architecture, and wrong-ABI package files.

Malformed archives/manifests (truncated tar, missing required v2 fields name/version/builtin/abi/arch/sha256, bad sha256) are rejected.
Wrong-architecture ELF (e_machine != x86_64 or ELFCLASS32) and wrong-ABI (abi != bash-5.3/any) packages are rejected.

Data-tree replacement on reinstall/upgrade-in-place preserves unrelated entries.
A failing install (e.g. corrupt payload member or failing pre-install step) rolls back to the exact previous tree.
Explicit 'pkg rollback TXN' and 'pkg remove NAME' restore/remove exactly the package's files and state, preserving unrelated entries.

deferrals.purpose: Deferred check of lone ESC grace, delayed continuation, ambiguous exact-prefix sequences, and the max(400 ms, ESCDELAY*8) total cap.
deferrals.reason: Remaining obligations: r4: Not reachable through the candidate interface: the fixed wgetch.c bw_keys table (no fixture or terminfo loading) contains no exact key that is also a prefix of a longer key (e.g. ESC[20~ and ESC[200~ diverge at byte 5), so the exact-vs-longer resolution path in bw_read_key_fd cannot be triggered by any input. Requires a candidate key-table extension, not a fixture.; r5: Not observable: the longest wgetch key is 6 bytes and the cap timer starts after the second byte, so at most 4 further bytes each within one 50 ms slice arrive in under 200 ms, below the 400 ms minimum cap; any slower trickle ends on the 50 ms slice first. The cap can never be the deciding condition with the fixed table (kgetch's fixture-extensible table is covered by migration-kgetch-total-cap-*).
remaining_requirements: Ambiguous exact-prefix sequences (an exact key that is also a prefix of a longer key) resolve to the exact key when no further byte arrives within the 50 ms inter-byte slice, and to the longer key when it does.
The total sequence cap is max(400 ms, ESCDELAY*8): bytes trickled below the slice interval stop being accepted once the cap elapses.
deferrals.resolution: See the requirement-level deferral review and execution evidence.
